headline: Belhaven leads overall wins yet trails in conference
dek: Belhaven scored 42 goals while conceding 30, the only positive overall goal difference in the CCS, and its eight wins topped every conference rival. Three draws and seven losses still left the program behind Asbury and Covenant once conference play settled the standings.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: High scoring did not translate into control for Piedmont: 45 goals scored was outpaced by 56 conceded, leaving the conference's most prolific attack with eleven losses against seven wins and one draw.

wire.line: Huntingdon went winless with four draws and four losses, scoring six goals and conceding thirteen.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Piedmont freshman Daris Mustic scored sixteen goals and added two assists on 35 shots.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Asbury goalkeeper Tolan Beaty recorded 61 saves against nineteen goals allowed for a 0.763 save percentage, while posting three shutouts.

findings.label: derived
findings.text: At least eighteen different players scored for Belhaven this season, spreading its offense across the roster.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Four matches on the CCS schedule passed their scheduled dates without a published result: Asbury's games against Johnson Tennessee and Kentucky Christian, plus both meetings between Belhaven and Millsaps.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Covenant midfielder Henry Parker paired five goals with seven assists on 25 shots.

last_match.line: Covenant entered the match after back-to-back wins over Huntingdon and Piedmont, while Lynchburg repeated its earlier victory over the same opponent.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
